claims.text: Fixed EAM reference potentials inadequately represent the variety of atomic configurations in ab initio liquids.

Replacing fixed EAM references with an actively learned machine-learning potential trained on liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
An active-learning workflow can construct and update a moment-tensor or deep-neural-network potential using ab initio data.
The potential can be updated on the fly during ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The training set will include representative liquid configurations together with solid-state data.
Actively learned moment-tensor potentials parameterized with ab initio data have been used for refractory multi-principal-element alloys.
A deep neural-network potential has described both solid and liquid states of high-entropy Ti-Zr-Ta-Hf-Nb carbonitrides.
The proposed method applies to refractory high-entropy alloys with at least five principal elements.
The applicable temperature regime is at or above 0.8 of the melting temperature, generally 2000–3600 K.
Ab initio liquids in this regime exhibit rich configurational diversity.
A flexible machine-learning potential can provide a representative mapping of the potential-energy surface across both solid and liquid phases.
The machine-learning potential improves that mapping by capturing many-body interactions and high configurational entropy.
Active learning identifies high-uncertainty configurations and adds them to the training set.
Adding high-uncertainty configurations ensures accurate representation of both rare and common atomic arrangements.
The intervention could decrease thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The magnitude of improvement depends on active-learning quality, alloy composition, and coverage of liquid configurations.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% statistically significant mismatch reduction together with improved phase-space overlap would falsify the hypothesis.

The comparison should use the same refractory high-entropy alloy, temperature range, and integration protocol for the EAM and machine-learning references, with direct ab initio results at representative state points.
